transcription:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-27 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood), Claire Huang (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Nimbus), Carlos Ruiz (Nimbus), Lena Park (Nimbus)
Shared: caching-benchmarks.xlsx (link in chat), staging logs bucket: s3://nimbus-staging-logs (note)

[00:00] Samir: All right folks, thanks for joining, this is our weekly POC caching sync. Quick agenda  Claire will walk through the latest hit-rate numbers, then we'll discuss prompt reuse strategies and define experiments.
[00:23] Claire: Cool, I'll share my screen, um there is a slide with per-route KV and prefix hit rates. Note  transcription may be off if I say KV cache or maybe K V cache, sorry.
[00:40] Claire: So overall on the product_reco route we saw a KV cache hit rate of about 62% last week, prefix cache hit around 48%. On support_chat route it's lower  KV ~34%, prefix ~29%. The benchmark sheet has the breakdown by user cohort and sequence length.
[01:12] Carlos: Quick Q  when you say prefix cache hit, is that the normalized prompt or exact string match? Because we have pretty noisy user messages.
[01:20] Claire: Great question  current prefix caching is mostly exact prefix match after minimal whitespace normalization. So we get low reuse when prompt wording varies.
[01:32] Maya: That's what we suspected. Our product_reco prompts do have a lot of template variables, but we do expect repeated prefixes for returning users.
[01:45] Claire: We ran a couple of toy canonicalization experiments  trimming stop tokens, lowercasing, and removing ephemeral IDs  this bumped prefix hit from 48% to about 57% for the sampled 5k requests. But it also changed some outputs slightly, we saw a small drop in relevance score for a subset.
[02:10] Lena: How are you measuring relevance? Is that automatic eval or manual?
[02:15] Claire: It's a mix  quick heuristic similarity score plus a handful of manual checks on top-ranked results. The sheet flags those changes.
[02:30] Samir: Another lever is sticky-prefix caching  bucket by hashed user id so repeated sessions for same user reuse KV cache. That helped other customers in our Dedicated trials.
[02:44] Carlos: We have privacy constraints; we can't store plain PII in cache keys. But we can hash user ids  may need to confirm with security if salted hashing is allowed.
[02:55] Maya: Also need to be careful with TTLs, some of our users' contexts change quickly.
[03:05] Claire: Right  current TTL for KV cache is 10 minutes in staging. For product_reco we might increase to 30 min for returning sessions, but test for staleness.
[03:18] Claire: The bench results show latency improvements when hit rate increases  median token latency drops ~18% when KV hit rate moves from 40% to 70%, and overall token cost per request drops accordingly.
[03:40] Carlos: Any concerns about KV cache size or memory pressure? The staging instances are mid-sized.
[03:46] Claire: With current traffic, memory is fine; biggest issue is fragmentation from many unique prefixes. We can do prefix bucketing or canonicalization to reduce cardinality. Also consider LRU vs LFU policies.
[04:05] Samir: For the POC next experiments we're proposing two parallel runs: A) prompt canonicalization pipeline before hitting the runtime and B) sticky-prefix bucketing by hashed user partition. Both targeted to product_reco route first.
[04:25] Maya: Sounds reasonable. For canonicalization, can you share the transform rules? We worry about changing semantics.
[04:32] Claire: Yes  rules will be conservative: remove request-ids, strip trailing punctuation in template slots, collapse repeated whitespace, lowercase english letters. We'll tag transformations so we can roll back. 
[04:48] Lena: Also, what about prompt reuse at the client SDK level? We have some reuse in web front-end already.
[04:55] Samir: Good point  dedupe at multiple layers helps. We'll coordinate with your SDK team.
[05:10] Claire: One weird thing in logs  tokenization boundary differences cause mismatches in prefix keys, particularly with emojis and non-ascii product names. We should normalize to Unicode NFC and strip control chars. That improved matches in a small test.
[05:30] Carlos: Ok, we'll ensure staging log extract includes raw prompt and normalized prompt so you can compare.
[05:38] Claire: Also noticed that when using quantized models in Dedicated testbed, KV cache semantics differ slightly because of generation variances; may cause some evictions. We logged a few cases.
[05:55] Maya: I flagged those in the bench sheet.
[06:05] Samir: Let's talk hit-rate goals  what would be meaningful for you?
[06:12] Maya: If we can get product_reco KV hit to above 75% and prefix above 65% without harming relevance we consider that a win.
[06:20] Claire: Based on current lift, canonicalization got us to 57% prefix; combining with sticky-prefix should plausibly reach low 70s. We'll need the experiments.
[06:35] Lena: Anything else in the data  cold start vs warm user differences?
[06:40] Claire: Yeah cold sessions have near-zero prefix reuse; warm returning sessions dominate the good hit rates. That's why bucket-by-user helps.
[06:50] Carlos: We'll prepare a sample of returning-session traffic for the experiment.
[07:00] Samir: On instrumentation  Claire will provide a small snippet to log cache hits/misses with request_id, normalized_prompt, raw_prompt (redacted) and route; please add to staging.
[07:12] Claire: I'll drop the snippet in the chat and commit to the repo. It will include options to toggle verbosity.
[07:20] Carlos: One thing  we saw occasional misattribution in the transcript here but in logs it looks fine.
[07:25] Samir: (laughs) yeah fireflies sometimes calls me Speaker 3.

[07:40] Claire: Quick note on measurement  please keep a consistent window for stats (we used 7-day sliding), and ensure sample sizes >5k for statistical confidence. Small cohorts give noisy numbers.
[07:52] Maya: Understood. We'll keep 7-day windows.

[08:10] Samir: Any blockers from the Nimbus side?
[08:15] Carlos: Only the debug logs toggle and confirmation on hashed user id approach  security wants to review.
[08:20] Maya: I'll loop in security after this meeting.

[08:30] Claire: Final recap  experiments A and B, instrumentation snippet, staging logs upload, and Samir shares annotated bench sheet. We'll reconvene next week to review results and if signals look good, plan a short pilot expansion to higher traffic.

[08:50] Samir: Great. Thanks everyone. I'll send a follow-up with the timeline.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcript contains occasional disfluencies and slight speaker mislabels (common in automated meeting exports). See caching-benchmarks.xlsx for full metric tables and flagged examples (link in Slack).
